title: Telltale Hooks record v1
description: Host envelope written once per hook observation. Detection content is carried only as unmodified Telltale ActionRecordV1 values (validate those with Telltale's action-record-v1 schema or ActionRecordV1::from_json). See docs/adr/0005-telemetry-envelope.md.

telltale_rev.description: Digest of the Telltale package version and the build Git hash that wrote the record; not a Git object name.

tool_name.description: The tool name as the harness reported it (for example Copilot `view`), never the normalized evaluation encoding.

input_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of the tool input as the harness reported it, before any normalization of the evaluation encoding.

lock_wait_ms.description: How long the call waited for its session's lock, over every time it took it, in milliseconds: time spent behind the session's other calls, apart from `build_ms` and `scan_ms`. Absent from records written before 2026-11.

history.description: The scan of the session history with the line a call past the projection budget is journaled as, after its pieces; `refused` when Telltale failed that source or quarantined the call's line; null when the call was not past the budget or had no history. Absent from records written before 2026-11.

returned_verdict.description: Present only when the verdict returned to the harness differs from `verdict`: an `ask` returned as `deny` because the harness cannot put an ask to a human (Codex CLI, OpenCode v1, OpenCode v2 --auto). Never `allow`. Added 2026-11 (ADR 0004 addendum).

grant.description: Present only when a grant the user gave in the session covered the call: nothing was returned (`returned` is false), `verdict`, `basis` and the scores are the policy's, and the session's score and attempts were left as they were (`session_score_after` equals `session_score_before`). `scope` is the grant's: `once` and `session` grants are given in the session, `project` and `user` grants are files in `grants.d` of the user's configuration root. `granted_by` is the record ID of the `grant` lifecycle record that made a `once` or `session` grant, and the grant ID of a `project` or `user` grant. Added 2026-11.

prior_returned_verdict.description: Present only when the decision returned a different verdict than `prior_verdict` (an `ask` returned as `deny`); `enforcement` is accounted against it. Added 2026-11 (ADR 0004 addendum).

lifecycle.description: Event-specific, content-free lifecycle details, named by `event`. A `grant` record (the user's grant line allowed a stopped call) has `scope` (`once` or `session`), `tool` (the stopped call's tool name), `rule_ids` (its detections, sorted) and `offer_record_id` (its decision record); a decision record a grant covers names this record in `decision.grant.granted_by`. A `grant` record written by `telltale hooks allow` (a project or user grant in `grants.d`) has `scope` (`project` or `user`), `tool`, `rule_ids`, `offer_record_id` (the decision record it was made from), `grant_id` (the file's grant ID, which a covered call's `decision.grant.granted_by` names) and, for `project`, `project_sha256` (SHA-256 of the project directory as written in the grant; never the path); `telltale hooks revoke` writes a `grant_revoked` record with `grant_id`. Both have `hook_event` `terminal`, an empty `session_id` and the grant's harness (empty when a revoked file names none). A `grant_refused` record has `cause`: `not_user_prompt` (the prompt event may not be the user's own: a subagent's, or on a harness that cannot take a grant line) or `no_offer` (no stopped call can be allowed). Neither carries the prompt, a pattern, matched text or a path. Added 2026-11.

pinned_over.description: On `session_start` records: the sources whose different value a pin on the hook command (`--state-dir`, `--user-config-dir`) replaced in the launch of the hook invocation that received the event, by name only (an environment variable such as `TELLTALE_HOOKS_STATE_DIR`, or a settings key such as `hooks.state_dir`), sorted; never a value. Absent when no pin replaced anything. Added 2026-11.

error_code.description: Content-free code. On `error` records: why the hook could not do its job. On `outcome` records: `outcome_ambiguous`, a result reported under a synthetic correlation key (`tth-syn-`) that only matched an already settled call; it may belong to that call or to a later identical one, so `result` is `unknown` and the settlement it supersedes is neither confirmed nor contradicted. It is followed by a second outcome for the same tool_use_id carrying the reported result with `enforcement: no_decision`: the execution happened, no decision is known to apply. A consumer keeping the latest outcome per tool_use_id sees that `no_decision` record (ADR 0004 addendum, point 11).

lock_wait_ms.description: On `error` records of a call that tried to take its session's lock: how long it waited for it, in milliseconds, up to giving up for `state_lock_timeout`. Added 2026-11.

telltale.description: Telltale ActionRecordV1 values anchored at this observation, unmodified. They describe the evaluation encoding, which for non-Claude harnesses is the normalized form of the call (ADR 0002 addendum), so their `tool_name` and facets may differ from `action` (for example `Read` for Copilot `view`, or `Write` with a path for a patch). Their `client` and `source_id` are those of the call's harness (`claude`/`claude.hooks`, `codex`/`codex.hooks`, `copilot`/`copilot.hooks`).

destinations.description: Where an exfil.outbound_upload action sends, as its command text says (DestinationFacts). Present only on such actions; it never changes the record, scores or verdicts. Entries are sorted in ascending byte order, which this schema cannot express; `DestinationFacts::is_valid` checks it with the entry structure.
